claims.statement: commit_note() in src/hypermnesic/commit_note.py is the single sanctioned corpus write, ordered guard → frontmatter gate → file write → per-path git commit (and push) → index projection → audit, with git as the only synchronous durability layer and embeddings explicitly asynchronous so they never block a write.

The path guard (serialize.check) runs before the target file is read and before the body is touched, so a protected path is refused before any content work; the default write surface is blocklist mode (allowlist=None, protected-path refusal plus governance fence as the sole bound) and an explicit allowlist only narrows it.

The durable unit of a write is a real commit, not a staged change: commit_note writes the file, stages only that path (`git add -- <rel>`) and commits it (`git commit -q -m <msg> -- <rel>`), which is what makes the write recoverable from HEAD alone.

A process-local advisory lock (serialize.index_write_lock on .hypermnesic/index.lock) is held around the locked write section, but it provides no cross-process exclusion between committers — the path-scoped git operations are the isolation mechanism.

The diff-or-die frontmatter gate computes the new file text in memory and raises FrontmatterDriftError for any unrequested frontmatter change, so a gate abort leaves the file byte-identical, HEAD unmoved, and no index row or audit entry written.

Drift detection compares frontmatter as per-key line blocks so an addition, a removal and a reordering all count as drift, and prefers a surgical in-place scalar line edit that leaves every other byte untouched, falling back to a ruamel round-trip for structural edits; results that would reflow untouched keys abort rather than churn.

A file with no frontmatter accepts a body replacement, but setting or deleting frontmatter fields on it raises ValueError("no frontmatter to edit"); the MCP tool catches that input-shape error with the guard and gate errors and returns a clean refusal instead of a raw tool traceback.

When a git remote exists, the write path converges before writing: fetch plus fast-forward to the remote tip (a non-fast-forwardable divergence is a refusal, never a merge) followed by serialize.preflight(expected_head=base), which raises HeadDriftError when HEAD moved past the base captured for this write.

Push is retried on a non-fast-forward by fetching and rebasing the single commit onto the advanced tip, bounded by the module constant _PUSH_MAX_ATTEMPTS; on an unrecoverable failure (conflict, auth/network error, rejecting hook, exhausted retries) the code fetches, resets --hard to the remote tip to drop the local-ahead commit, and raises GitCoordinationError so no un-pushed commit can wedge a fast-forward-only puller.
The new SHA is re-read after the push because a retry rebase rewrites the commit id, so the SHA returned to the caller and recorded in the audit entry is the one that actually landed.

Every git operation in the write is path-scoped (staging, the nothing-staged check and the commit all name the note's path), so an unrelated change another committer has staged on a shared checkout is never swept into this commit or pushed; rename_note scopes its commit to the moved pair for the same reason.

Idempotence: content identical to what is already on disk, and the case where staging leaves nothing staged for that path, both return a CommitResult with noop=True, no commit and no audit entry, and the staged check is path-scoped so foreign staged work cannot turn a no-op into a commit.

A refusal is never a silent success and never leaves a partial write: at the library boundary refusals raise (serialize.WriteGuardError, FrontmatterDriftError, serialize.HeadDriftError, GitCoordinationError, and ValueError for gate input-shape problems), the MCP write tool converts each into an explicit hand-built CallToolResult carrying {"committed": false, "refused": ...} that survives HTTP structured-output validation, and no file, commit, index row or audit entry results.

When auth is enabled the MCP write tool self-enforces the write OAuth scope from the authenticated principal, independently of the transport's global required_scopes, refusing before any write; the refusal tells the client to reconnect and approve write access and states that approval does not bypass the protected-path, frontmatter, head-drift, audit or git-coordination guards.

A failure to project a landed commit into the index is reported as a degraded success rather than an error: CommitResult carries the real new_sha with index_degraded=True and a stable degraded_reason (index_write_failed for a sqlite error, else index_error: type: message), the audit entry is still written because it records the git write, and the tool tells callers to keep the returned SHA and not rewrite the note.

The projection performed synchronously during a write is lexical only — the path's chunk and full-text rows are replaced and its doc-surface vector is invalidated — while dense embedding is asynchronous, so a newly written note is findable lexically immediately and its vectors catch up through read-time convergence.

Every landed write appends one JSONL entry {ts, actor, verb, path, old_sha, new_sha, summary} to .hypermnesic/audit.jsonl; the actor is server-set from a verified node identity or a fixed sentinel with caller-supplied actors ignored, and summaries are truncated to MAX_SUMMARY so a full page body is never recorded.

The audit log defines a separate body-free refusal event (verb "refusal" with attempted_verb, category and a token-redacted summary) that the owner-facing audit view renders alongside writes, but commit_note never writes one — a refused write leaves the log empty, so a refusal can never be mistaken for a write.

AuditLog.reconcile(repo) back-fills entries for commits between the last logged new_sha and HEAD as verb "reconcile" entries, making a crash between commit and log append recoverable rather than permanent; it is an explicit engine operation rather than an automatic side effect of a write.

rename_note is the atomic move surface: the guard runs on both source and destination, an optional content edit goes through the frontmatter gate first so a gate abort means no git operation happens, the optional tombstone sink is invoked with the neutral repo-relative old path after the gate and before the removing git operation, and the move commits only the moved pair before re-keying the index without re-embedding.
An index failure during a rename is the same degraded success as a note write: the rename's SHA is returned with index_degraded set and the rename audit entry is still appended.

The CLI `hypermnesic commit-note` is a dry-run preview by default with no file, commit, index or audit effect that still runs the path guard and the frontmatter gate, while `--commit` performs the real guarded write and wires the index projection when <repo>/.hypermnesic/index.db exists, with --json reporting new_sha.
Only the MCP write tool supplies an audit log; a commit landed through the CLI or the library carries no inline audit entry and is instead back-fillable from HEAD by the log reconciler.

prepose's immutable free-append fast path commits new files straight to HEAD by calling commit_note, while any change that is not a new file in an append zone is gated in memory first and committed as one atomic commit on a hypermnesic/proposals/<slug> branch inside an isolated worktree that never touches the owner's live HEAD and is never auto-merged.

Memory-control forget and revert are the deliberate exception to the single call path: they reuse serialize.check, the single-writer lock and the stricter preflight(require_clean=True) clean-tree guard but perform their own path-scoped git rm/git revert commits, append their own audit verbs, and refuse rather than guess on anything more complex than a single-file markdown change.

Changes to commit_note.py, serialize.py or frontmatter_gate.py are security-sensitive: they are CODEOWNERS-routed and must cite SECURITY.md and docs/threat-model-commit-note.md in the same PR, with the threat model kept as the living artifact of record whose dated review deltas are append-only.

The write path is composed by injection rather than global state — commit_note takes repo, path, body, set_fields, summary, idx, log, allowlist and dry_run from the caller (idx=None or log=None skips that step), rename_note additionally takes a tombstone_fn seam, and push retry depth is the module constant _PUSH_MAX_ATTEMPTS rather than an operator-visible config knob.

Write-path state lives in the target repo's .hypermnesic/ dir (index.lock, audit.jsonl, index.db) and the engine ignores that dir through .git/info/exclude, never by editing the vault's tracked .gitignore.
